decision: Allow a file owner to explicitly enable a revocable anonymous media URL for each completed download.
rationale: The product owner requested directly shareable media URLs with an opaque identifier and readable file name, and explicitly accepted public access by possession of the link.
controls: Only the authenticated owner can enable, revoke, or rename a shared file, and every mutation requires CSRF validation.
The 192-bit URL token is HMAC-derived from a per-installation key and random per-download nonce; only a SHA-256 token hash is stored in SQLite.
Resolved file paths remain inside the configured download directory, extensions cannot change during rename, and invalid links return a generic 404.
Revocation or file deletion invalidates the link; old file-name paths redirect only while the underlying token remains active.
Media responses are inline, support HTTP byte ranges, and disable caching. Application access logging is disabled to avoid recording capability URLs.
consequences: Anyone possessing an active URL can access that media without an account.
Operators must protect reverse-proxy logs and backups containing the persistent share-signing key.
Restoring `/data` without its matching `/downloads` content, or vice versa, may leave unusable link records until queue history is cleaned up.
